content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"General is short-staffed: 11 agents on phones against 16 planned (-31%), and service level fell to about 35% in the last two intervals. Attendance explains the gap. General has 12 absences against a usual 2.4 per day: 4 called in sick and 8 were sent home unwell by team leads, logged through 15:20. Volume is only modestly above forecast (+4.8% for the day), so this is not mainly a demand surge. There is no relevant incident (only a branch printer issue) and no marketing entry. Payments is close to plan, and its service level dipped to 70.6% at 19:45.","plan_name":"No further intraday actions: end of operating day","rationale":"It is now 20:00, the end of the planning horizon, so no window remains for any lever. Overtime would arrive 30 minutes after approval and outside operating hours. Break delays, coaching cancellations, cross-skill moves, callback and deflection would all need a window after now. Payments could not donate agents anyway, since it is at 70.6%, the 70% floor. The earlier response for general was already broad: break delays, coaching cancelled to 20:00, five overtime offers, IVR callback and chat deflection. Recommended follow-up for tomorrow: check how many of the 8 agents sent home are fit to work, raise general's shrinkage assumption if illness is spreading, and pre-book overtime or cross-skill cover before the day starts.","actions":[]}
